name: John Munro
role: Medora bartender, cigar seller and later Mingusville stockman
bio: John 'Johnny' Munro took a contract in January 1885 to cut a hundred cords of wood for the stage line, mostly in the Cave Hills country. In 1885 he ran the bar at the Northern Pacific Hotel, advertised El Mapa Mundi and Republic cigars, and put up a thousand tons of hay on the Big Plateau with the Gifford brothers. He married Anne Brophy at the Catholic church in August 1885, and that October he went into the sheep business on his own near Mingusville. In 1886 the paper announced the birth of a son, William, and reported that he had bought the Osborne brothers' Æ cattle brand while holding the Culbertson & Weeks ranch on Beaver Creek.
